    - tool: "Skill"
      argument: "{\"skill\":\"headwater-authoring\",\"args\":\"Write a new decision record (kind: decision, shelf docs/decisions/) that rules: harper-core becomes part of the engine, as an advisory backend, triggered by an adopter's request. This supersedes HW-DR-0096 (docs/decisions/0096-harper-does-not-become-part-of-the-engine-now-and-q41-stands.md), which ruled that harper-core does NOT become part of the engine now. The new decision must declare `supersedes: HW-DR-0096` so the engine writes the inverse `superseded_by` edge on 0096. Base the rationale on the context already in the corpus: HW-DR-0096's own reopening condition (\\\"An adopter asks... that adopter's corpus is the sample\\\") and the measurements in docs/evaluations/harper-spike-results.md (0/187 hand-read findings were true errors on this corpus's own sample; two rules — doubled-word and wrong-article — are the only categories Harper adds that the engine lacks; cost of 496 crates and a rustc floor conflict at version 2.11.0+; advisory-only categories identified in that spike: AnA, SpellCheck for regional spelling, CompoundNouns, DisjointPrefixes, DiscourseMarkers, OxfordComma, Codebase, WouldNeverHave, and the three Expand* rules). Advisory backend means Harper's findings are surfaced to the requesting adopter but are not promoted to controls/autofix in this engine by default — i.e., it does not change spec 00's grammar exclusion for every adopter, only integrates Harper as an optional advisory source gated on that adopter's own corpus meeting whatever bar they request, per HW-DR-0096's own reopening condition. Do not invent new measurements; cite the existing evaluation page. Follow the decision kind's required facets (status, status_since, summary, last_verified, title) and required sections (Context, Decision, Consequences), as shown by `headwater explain` on HW-DR-0096. Pick the next available decision number/id and a title that follows this corpus's existing title style (numbered, descriptive). Write the file and run `headwater check --fix --root .` then `headwater check --root .` afterward, fixing anything it flags on the files touched.\"}"

    - tool: "Skill"
      argument: "{\"skill\":\"headwater-authoring\",\"args\":\"Write a new obligation_record documenting debt that docs/decisions/0112-the-additive-campaign-measures-eleven-actions-by-five-layers-in-seven-scenarios.md deferred but never recorded anywhere. In its \\\"The circumstance axes\\\" section, HW-DR-0112 says: \\\"Three axes are deferred and recorded as debt: corpus size, tasks outside anything a document governs, and an adopter's own repository.\\\" This task is specifically about the THIRD of those three deferred axes: an adopter's own repository (i.e. the campaign's probes and scenarios all run against this repository's own corpus, never against a repository that merely adopted the Headwater package/standard — so nothing measures whether the five layers, eleven actions, and seven scenarios generalize to an adopter's repository rather than this one). The other two deferred axes (corpus size; tasks outside anything a document governs) are out of scope for this record — do not fold them in, they are not \\\"recorded anywhere\\\" either but this task is scoped to the adopter's-own-repository axis only.\\n\\nCreate a new obligation_record (kind confirmed via MCP: shelf docs/obligations/**, required facets status, status_since, summary, last_verified, title, waiting_on; required sections Context, Obligation, Discharge) that records this as outstanding debt, following the shape and voice of existing docs/obligations/*.md records (e.g. HW-OBL-0183). Determine the next free HW-OBL sequence number and filename slug following this corpus's conventions (the highest currently used is HW-OBL-0242; obligation files are named NNNN-slug.md under docs/obligations/). Write the actual file.\"}"
